newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close with signs of rebound.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close with signs of rebound.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended the day higher on Wednesday as fund managers and punters began accumulating stocks on recent falls, analysts said.
The benchmark composite index was up 4.36 at 1139.32, while the Second Board index bounced back to close 20.39 points up at 588.84.

"News that the Ekran signing ceremony is going to take place later today has taken away much of the uncertainty surrounding some of the stocks connected to the Bakun dam project," said Razani Radzi, research manager at PB Securities.
Ekran stock closed up 40 cents at 11.50 on news of the signing ceremony as well as a statement released by the company on Wednesday afternoon that it is going to retain control of the project.
"It looks like foreign funds have been buying Malaysian blue-chips stocks today," said Razani. "Sime Darby and Genting have both seen a fair amount of buying action," he added.
Sime Darby was up 5 cents at 8.40 ringgit with 5.2 million shares traded, while Genting was up 40 at 18.90.
Volumes were high with 218.5 million shares traded valued at 1,838 million ringgit. Gainers outpaced losers 407 to 174.
